note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Severe, progressive headache for ~3 days. No clear trigger or exposure reported.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset ~3 days ago, started gradually while at work; worse by next morning and has progressively increased.
  - Pain is present most of the time with fluctuating intensity; current severity ~8/10.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: none.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: none.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: none.
  - Drooling: none.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: photophobia/light sensitivity; reported “weird shooting lights”; pain mainly around the right eye.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: none.
  - Dyspnea: none.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): none reported.
  - Ear symptoms/hearing changes: none.
  - Neck pain/swelling: none; no neck stiffness.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Past headaches previously responsive to ibuprofen.
  - Patient reports she has never personally had a migraine; family history positive for migraines (mother with severe seasonal migraines; sister with less frequent migraine).
  - No reported prior ED visits or injections documented.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: “not that I know of.”
  - Regular medications: none reported.
  - Current/rescue medications: patient has been taking ibuprofen (patient reported “three a day”; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Additional medications discussed/offered by clinician: Naproxen — dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented; Codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Relevant social context:
  - Lives with three housemates.
  - Works in IT (extensive computer use); reduced screen brightness due to symptoms.
  - Wears glasses since childhood.
  - Social smoker and social alcohol use.
  - No accompaniment/supervision stated.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: no swelling of lips, tongue, face, or uvula documented.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: no stridor or respiratory distress documented.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Patient alert but “hard to focus.”
  - Reports feeling “sick” with headache but no vomiting.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression: Probable migraine-like headache.
  - Justification: progressive unilateral/periorbital (right eye) pain with photophobia and visual “shooting lights,” family history of migraines, prior headaches responsive to NSAIDs, current poor response to ibuprofen.
- Conflict noted: none identified in transcript.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Discussed optimizing analgesia: adjust ibuprofen dosing (doctor stated patient can take up to two tablets three times a day; specific tablet strength not documented).
  - Discussed prescribing stronger analgesia options: Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented); consideration of adding Paracetamol or Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented). Clinician indicated they can provide a prescription today.
  - Advised to reduce screen brightness and consider an eye test if eye strain suspected.
- Specific instructions provided to patient:
  - “If your headaches aren't getting any better, or they're getting worse. Um, you know, I want you to give me a call, or come back and see me sooner. OK?”
  - “If you're having any problems with your vision, or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well. Just give me a call, and come back and see me.”
- Escalation criteria / red flags:
  - New or worsening vision problems, focal neurological weakness (arms/legs), significant clinical deterioration, or increasing/severe headache not responsive to analgesia — return promptly or contact clinician as above.
- Follow-up:
  - Return visit arranged/planned in approximately 1–2 weeks to reassess.
  - If headaches become more frequent, discussion of prophylactic preventive medications at follow-up.
  - Keep a headache diary to identify triggers and patterns.
- Other:
  - No ENT/allergy referral was explicitly arranged during this consult.
  - No emergency medications or devices (e.g., epinephrine auto-injector) were discussed or required based on this transcript.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, RR, temperature, O2 saturation) not recorded.
  - Focused ENT and neurologic examination findings (cranial nerves, fundoscopy, focal neuro exam) not recorded.
  - Exact doses, routes, and frequencies for ibuprofen taken by patient and for any prescriptions (naproxen, paracetamol, codeine) not documented.
  - Any prior imaging (CT/MRI) or prior ED evaluations not documented.
  - Formal migraine diagnostic criteria review and clear documentation of mechanical/ocular causes not present.
  - Allergy reconciliation beyond patient report not documented.
  - Explicit prescription details and whether prescriptions were issued today not clearly documented (clinician stated they could provide a prescription).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall clear; occasional filler speech and pauses. No significant background noise or inaudible sections noted.
